chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Al-Khizr (peace be upon him) said to Musa (peace be upon him): 'O Musa! The best of your days is the one that is in front of you, so see which day it is and prepare your answer for it, for you will be paused and questioned. Take your lesson from time, for time is long yet short. So work as if you can see the reward of your deed, so that it may make you more hopeful for the Hereafter, for whatever is coming from the world is like what has already passed from it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the advice of Al-Khizr to Musa regarding the best day and preparing for the Hereafter?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Al-Khizr advises Musa (AS) to prioritize the immediate future as the most critical period for accountability, urging him to prepare for the divine pause and questioning. This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *al-amal al-salih* (righteous action) driven by hope in the Hereafter, using the paradox of time being both long and short to encourage mindfulness. The advice highlights that the transient nature of worldly affairs should motivate believers to act as if they already witness the rewards of their deeds.
